concept_summary: Club Deluxe bar at 1511 Haight Street proposes to intensify an existing bar and nighttime entertainment use with live amplified music to 2 a.m., amending conditions of the 1996 Conditional Use Authorization that approved non-amplified entertainment at this address.

overall.line: Of the 5 approvals this concept needs: 2 further review (zoning and use, entertainment permit), 2 insufficient information (alcohol licence, building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning to amend the 1996 approval conditions, with a pre-application meeting presenting soundproofing measures, patron management plan, and community liaison commitment before submitting the formal CUA package.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is the original 1996 Conditional Use Authorization for this exact address (1501-1509 Haight/609 Ashbury), which approved a place of entertainment for non-amplified music in the Haight Street NCD. The concept seeks to amend this approval's conditions, making it the most directly relevant precedent.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved entertainment at this site in 1996 with non-amplified music only. Subsequent referrals in 2016-2017 (Type 48 license, Place of Entertainment permit) confirmed continuation of this use. The 2017 health referral required the operator to abide by Motion No. 14221 conditions, establishing that amendments to these conditions would require Commission approval.

In addition, the operator shall be responsible for d aily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed -source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. Works at 415-554-.5810, http://sfdpw.org. (standard)

Notices Posted at Bars and Entertainment Venues: Notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion and to not litter or block driveways in the neighborhood, shall be well-lit and prominently displayed at all entrances to and exits from the establishment. For information about compliance, contact the Entertainment Commission, at 415 554 -6678, www.sfgov.org/entertainment (standard)

Other Entertainment: The Other Entertainment shall be performed within the enclosed building only. The building shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building and fixed -source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. Bass and vibrations shall also be contained within the enclosed structure. The Project Sponsor shall obtain all necessary approvals from the Entertainment Commission prior to operation. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Lighting: All Project lighting shall be directed onto the Project site and immediately surrounding sidewalk area only and designed and managed so as not to be a nuisance to adjacent residents. Nighttime lighting shall be the minimum necessary to ensure safety, but shall in no case be directed so as to constitute a nuisance to any surrounding property. (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Monitoring: The Project requires monitoring of the conditions of approval in this Motion. The Project Sponsor or the subsequent responsible parties for the Project shall pay fees as established under Planning Cod e Section 351(e) (1) and work with the Planning Department (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. (standard)

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service bar and restaurant at 1566 Haight (87m away, same NCD-HAIGHT district) that amended prior conditions to add entertainment and extend hours to 2 a.m. for bar use, approved December 2020. This is a use decision from a Planning Commission hearing showing how amendments to prior approvals are handled on this corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved 2 a.m. bar hours but imposed strict conditions: amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, soundproofing requirements, patron behavior notices at exits, community liaison, and Entertainment Commission approval before operation. The differential hours for restaurant (10 p.m.) vs bar (2 a.m.) show the Commission can split operating conditions by…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to amend previous authorization and add entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away, same district) was denied in April 1995. This is the only denial among nearby entertainment applications and occurred at the same address that was again denied entertainment in 2008.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission denied adding entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant on this corridor in 1995. The 2008 referral (MB0800611) confirmed this denial remained in effect 13 years later, showing the Commission's entertainment denials can create long-term restrictions on specific sites even when the underlying bar/restaurant use continues.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2008 referral documenting that the 1995 denial of Place of Entertainment at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away) remained in effect, with no new CUA filed. Same address as the 1994.633C denial, showing how denied entertainment uses are tracked over time.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning continued to deny entertainment at this site 13 years after the original 1995 denial, demonstrating that once entertainment is denied at a specific location in this district, subsequent attempts face significant precedent. The record explicitly notes no new CUA application had been filed, suggesting operators understood the denial would be difficult to overcome.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Entertainment Commission referral for Limited Live Performance permit at 1569 Haight (72m away, same NCD-HAIGHT district), approved March 2022 as accessory use to existing bar. This is an agency referral, not a use decision, but shows how entertainment can be approved when subordinate to the primary bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved Limited Live Performance as an accessory use to an existing bar under Section 703(d)(6), without requiring a full CUA hearing. This pathway is available for limited entertainment (200 sq ft performance area, ends by 10-11 p.m.) but would not fit a concept where live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m. is a primary feature, not accessory.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain the 1996 Motion No. 14221 conditions from SF Planning Department records unit to confirm what restrictions are currently in place.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request the full Motion No. 14221 for Case No. 1996.520C (approved October 24, 1996) for 1501-1509 Haight Street. The 2017 Health referral (2017-002299MIS) states that the bar must abide by these conditions, but the specific text is not in the records bundle. Knowing these conditions is necessary to frame the CUA application as an amendment and to identify which conditions the applicant seeks to modify (e.g., amplification, hours, performance area size).

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, clearly framing it as an amendment to the 1996 approval (Case No. 1996.520C, Motion No. 14221) and specifying which conditions are proposed to change (amplification, hours, performance area).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The application narrative should state: This is a request to amend the conditions of the October 24, 1996 Conditional Use Authorization (Case No. 1996.520C) for a place of entertainment, which approved non-amplified music only. We propose to add amplified live music and extend entertainment hours. Include the acoustic report, good-neighbor plan, proof of pre-application outreach, and letters of support from the neighborhood. Request differential conditions: amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends, mirroring the 2019 approval at 1566 Haight.

timeline_cost.notes: The ranges cover the three approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120-300 days, $3,100-$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment permit (45-120 days, $2,708-$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), and Health Permit to Operate (14-45 days for health plan check plus 14-45 days for permit, $828-$2,500 plan check and $470-$1,000 permit per catalog:sf.health_plan_check and catalog:sf.health_permit). The CUA and POE permit applications can run in parallel but the POE hearing typically waits for the Planning Commission to act, so the total time is roughly the CUA timeline plus the POE timeline (not a simple sum). The comparable CUA cases took 4 to 424 days from filing to approval (N=2 approved), but one of those (1996.520C, 50 days) was decided in 1996 under different procedures; the 2019 CUA at 1566 Haight took 424 days. The cost range excludes building permit fees (which depend on construction valuation and whether a change of occupancy is triggered), ABC licence fees (unknown pathway), business registration, sign permit, FOG permit, state fees, music licensing, and professional services (architect, acoustic engineer, legal). These figures are times and costs to approval; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal.

records_summary: 1511 Haight Street is in the Haight Street NCD where a bar is a conditional use on the first story, and falls within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict which requires conditional use for any new on-sale liquor establishment (Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57). The site has a long history: a Conditional Use Authorization for a place of entertainment for non-amplified music was approved in 1996 (Case No. 1996.520C), with subsequent approvals for a Place of Entertainment permit (2016) and a Type 48 license (2016, 2017) operating as Club Deluxe bar. The immediate area is saturated with alcohol uses: 21 food/drink businesses and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, triggering the undue concentration flag. Only one dated use decision has been recorded within 1,000 feet in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate.
data_gaps: The 1996 CUA conditions (Motion No. 14221) are referenced but the full text of conditions is not exposed in the records
ABC license conditions for the existing Type 48 at this address are not available in the records
No hearing transcripts or Commission discussion available for the 1995 and 2008 entertainment denials at 1576-1580 Haight to understand the reasons for disapproval
The base rate shows only 1 dated use decision in 10 years within 1,000 feet—insufficient to calculate a meaningful approval rate for bars or entertainment uses in this area
No records indicate whether the existing Club Deluxe bar is still actively operating or has closed, though the 2017 health referral suggests continued operation
